hindi: अब इसके बाद हम भेषज के कल्प की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the preparation (kalpa) of medicines (bheṣaja).
notes: Opening formula of the chapter. 'kalpa' is rendered 'preparation'; the chapter goes on to land, collection, storage and the five forms of preparation.

lines_deva: जांगले साधारणे वा देशे यथाकालं शिशिरातपपवनसलिलसेविते समे शुचौ प्रदक्षिणोदके श्मशानचैत्यदेवतायतनागारसभाश्चआरामवल्मीकोषरविरहिते कुशरोहिषास्तीर्णे स्निग्धकृष्णसुवर्णवर्णमधुरसुरभिमुत्तिके मृदावफालकृष्टेऽनुपहतेऽन्यैर्बलवत्तरैर्द्रुमैर्भेषजानि प्रशस्यंतइति सामान्यतो भूमिपरीक्षा

hindi: जांगल यानी रूखे खुले प्रदेश में, या साधारण प्रदेश में, ऋतु के अनुसार, शीत, धूप, वायु और जल से सेवित, समतल, शुद्ध, दाहिनी ओर जल बहने वाली, श्मशान, चैत्य, देवमन्दिर, घर और सभा से तथा बाग, दीमक की बांबी और ऊषर भूमि से रहित, कुश और रोहिष यानी सम्भवतः रूसा घास से ढकी, चिकनी, काली, सोने के रंग की, मीठी और सुगन्धित मिट्टी वाली, मुद्रित मृदावफाल अस्पष्ट है, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार हल से जोती हुई, दूसरे अधिक बलवान वृक्षों से अनुपहत भूमि में औषध प्रशस्त माने जाते हैं। यह सामान्य रूप से भूमि की परीक्षा है।
english: In a jāṅgala (dry, open country) or in a common region, according to the season, in land that is frequented by cold, sunshine, wind and water, level, clean, with water flowing to the right, free from cremation ground, shrine (caitya), temple, house and assembly hall, and from garden, anthill and saline soil, spread with kuśa grass (Desmostachya bipinnata) and rohiṣa grass (probably a fragrant Cymbopogon grass; disputed), with soil that is unctuous, black, golden-coloured, sweet and fragrant, ploughed (the printed 'mṛdāvaphāla' is unclear; on a conjectural reading, with a ploughshare), and not harmed by other, stronger trees: medicines are praised. Thus it is the general examination of land.

text_flags.why: possible: 'caā' leaves an uncontracted hiatus; sandhi would give 'cā'
possible: 'muttikā' is not a word; 'mṛttikā' (soil) fits the sense and the list of qualities
the opening 'mṛdāvaphāla-' is not a clear word; possibly 'mṛdu' + 'avaphāla' or 'mṛdā' (with clay); no firm correction offered
possible: the print joins praśasyante and iti with an ai junction that sandhi does not give; read as the verb praśasyante plus iti

notes:
Long single sentence; the locatives (jāṅgale ... bhūmau) all describe the land, and the verb is 'praśasyante' at the end ('are praised'). 'jāṅgala' is a technical term for dry, sparsely watered, open country (standard). kuśa = Desmostachya bipinnata (standard); rohiṣa = a fragrant grass, probably Cymbopogon (lemongrass type); disputed. 'mṛdāvaphālakṛṣṭe' is doubtful: the words kept are 'mṛdā' (probably gently, or with clay) and 'avaphāla' (unclear), 'ploughed' (kṛṣṭa) is sure; the reading is conjectural. 'sevite': 'frequented by' is taken literally. 'pradakṣiṇodaka' is taken as water flowing to the right (clockwise). 'sabhāścaārāma' shows a hiatus typo (see text_flags). 'iti' closes the statement ('thus ... general examination of land').
OPEN (05.08.2) [minor] split / mṛdāvaphālakṛṣṭe: GLOSSARY: an unrestorable printed word is kept unsplit in w with gloss "unclear". The draft splits the damaged opening into mṛdā + avaphāla-kṛṣṭe and glosses mṛdā as "probably gently or with clay", which presents a split the print does not support. Suggested: Keep as is only if the owner accepts a conjectural split; safer: one word "mṛdāvaphāla-kṛṣṭe" glossed unclear. Not patched because the checker joins words by token.
OPEN (05.08.2) [minor] hindi / दाहिनी ... ढकी: Hindi switches to feminine adjectives and supplies "भूमि" although the locatives agree with देश (m.); also "बहने" (flowing) is not in pradakṣiṇa-udaka ("with water to the right"); same "flowing" in English. Suggested: Optional: literal "दाहिनी ओर जल वाले" and drop "बहने"/"flowing"; owner to decide.

lines_deva: विशेषतस्त्वश्मवती स्थिरा गुर्वी श्यामा कृशस्थूलतृणा वृक्षसस्यप्राया स्वगुणभूयिष्ठा
lines_iast: viśeṣatastvaśmavatī sthirā gurvī śyāmā kṛśasthūlatṛṇā vṛkṣasasyaprāyā svaguṇabhūyiṣṭhā
hindi: विशेष रूप से पथरीली, स्थिर, भारी, श्याम, पतली और मोटी घास वाली, अधिकतर वृक्षों और सस्य वाली, अपने गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: In particular: stony, firm, heavy, dark, with thin and thick grass, mostly with trees and crops (sasya), abounding in its own quality.
notes:
The feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' (land) understood from 2; no verb. 'svaguṇa' is 'its own quality'; the text does not name the element here, but the following units name the water, fire, wind and space types, so this is probably the earth type (inferred, not stated). 'kṛśasthūlatṛṇā' = 'with thin and thick grass' taken literally.
OPEN (05.08.3) [minor] hindi / सस्य: Hindi leaves sasya untranslated while English gives "crops". Suggested: फसलों/पौधों

hindi: चिकनी, शीतल, पास में जल वाली, चिकनी घास, सस्य और कोमल पत्तों से भरपूर, श्वेत और जल के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: Unctuous, cool, with water near, mostly with unctuous grass, crops (sasya) and tender leaves, white, and abounding in the quality of water.

notes: Feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' understood. The type is presumably the water type (the quality is 'ambu' on the suggested reading); inferred. 'āsañjodakā' read as 'āsanna-udakā' (conjectural, see flag). The word 'komala' is split by a space in the print: the first token 'koma' and the second 'ladalaprāyā'. In the word list the broken word is shown joined with a trailing hyphen.

hindi: अनेक रंगों वाली, हल्के फूलों वाली, बहुत विरल पाण्डु वृक्षों की वृद्धि वाली और अग्नि के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: Of various colours, having light flowers, with a very sparse growth of pale trees, and abounding in the quality of fire.
notes: Feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' understood. 'pāṇḍu' is 'pale' (not 'yellow'). The type is the fire type ('agniguṇa'). 'laghupuṣpavatī' could be 'having small flowers' or 'light flowers'; the literal 'light' is kept.

words.gloss: thin, slight; hollow; saline soil; mostly

hindi: गधे और राख के रंग की, रूखी, अधिकतर तनु, कोटर और ऊषर वाली, थोड़े रस वाली वृद्धि से युक्त और वायु के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: Of the colour of a donkey and of ash, dry, mostly slight, hollow and saline, with a growth of little taste (rasa), and abounding in the quality of wind.
notes:
Feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' understood. 'rāsabhabhasmavarṇā' is read as 'colour of donkey and ash'. 'tanukoṭaroṣara' is read as three members (tanu, koṭara, ūṣara); the grouping (e.g. 'thin hollows') is uncertain. 'alparasaprarohā' = 'growth of little rasa (taste, sap)'. Wind type ('anilaguṇa').
OPEN (05.08.6) [minor] english / mostly slight, hollow and saline: Hindi reads tanu, koṭara, ūṣara as three nouns; English reads them as adjectives; the two languages disagree on the same compound. Suggested: Align the two (owner).

hindi: कोमल, समतल, गड्ढों वाली, अस्पष्ट रस वाले जल से युक्त, किनारों पर बड़े वृक्षों वाली, श्याम और आकाश के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली।
english: Soft, level, having pits, with water of indistinct taste (rasa), with great trees at its edges, dark, and abounding in the quality of space (ākāśa).

text_flags.why: possible: feminine of mṛdu is 'mṛdvī'
possible: 'śvaara' is not a word; 'śvabhra' (pit, hollow) fits the print shape and the sense

notes: Feminine adjectives agree with 'bhūmi' understood. Space type ('ākāśaguṇa'). 'śvabhravatī' is a conjectural reading (see flag). 'mahāparyantavṛkṣā' is read 'with great trees at the boundary'; 'paryanta' could also mean 'ending in' (ambiguous).

lines_deva: तत्रांबुपृथिवीगुणभूयिष्ठासु भूमिषु जातानि विरेचनानि बृंहणानि च शस्यंते
lines_iast: tatrāṃbupṛthivīguṇabhūyiṣṭhāsu bhūmiṣu jātāni virecanāni bṛṃhaṇāni ca śasyaṃte
hindi: उनमें जल और पृथ्वी के गुणों की प्रचुरता वाली भूमियों में उत्पन्न हुए, विरेचन और बृंहण यानी पुष्टिकारक प्रशस्त माने जाते हैं।
english: Among these, (ones) born in lands abounding in the qualities of water and earth are praised as purgative (virecana) and nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa).
notes: The subject 'jātāni' is a bare neuter plural 'born (ones)', that is the medicines of line 05.08.2; the noun is not stated. 'virecana' = purgation, taken as predicate adjectives. Earth and water types correspond to the types of lines 05.08.3 and 05.08.4 (inferred, not stated).

words.gloss: fire; wind; space; quality; most abundant

hindi: अग्नि, वायु और आकाश के गुणों की प्रचुरता वाली भूमियों में वमन के। सब गुणों से युक्त भूमियों में उभयतोभाग यानी दोनों ओर भाग वाले।
english: In (lands) abounding in the qualities of fire, wind and space: (ones) for vomiting (vamana). In (lands) endowed with all the qualities: both-way (ubhayatobhāga) ones.
notes:
line 05.08.9: Elliptical: 'jātāni' and 'praśasyante' carry over from line 05.08.8; no verb is supplied in the translation. 'bhūmiṣu' (lands) is understood from 8.
line 05.08.10: Elliptical (from 8 and 9). 'ubhayatobhāga' is a technical term, literally 'having a share on both sides'; it is commonly understood as acting both upward and downward (emetic and purgative); probable, not stated in the line. The 'both-way' rendering is kept literal.

hindi: आकाश के गुण की प्रचुरता वाली भूमियों में शमन करने वाले।
english: In (lands) abounding in the quality of space (ākāśa): pacifying (śamana) ones.
notes: Elliptical (verb and 'jātāni' from 8). 'śamana' = pacifying, palliative (not purgative or emetic).

hindi: इस प्रकार वे अत्यन्त बलवान होते हैं।
english: Thus (they) become the most powerful.
notes: The subject is the medicines (neuter plural), understood. 'balavattama' is the superlative of 'balavat'.

english: Among these, those which are born in their time, have attained full measure, taste (rasa), potency (vīrya) and smell, whose smell, colour, taste, touch and potency (prabhāva) have not been harmed by time, sunshine, mi (unclear), water, wind, weapons and creatures, whose roots are deep, and which stand in the northern direction.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mi' (printed) is not a word here; 'agni' (fire) is a conjecture only
possible: 'm' for 'n': 'prabhāvāny' (n. pl.) agrees with 'anupahata ... prabhāvāni'
the first letter 'u' is attached to the previous token 'mūlānyu'; the word is 'udīcyām'

notes: The relative clause 'yāni ... sthitāni' continues into line 05.08.14 ('teṣām'). words.gloss: to be taken, to be gathered

hindi: उनमें से, हाल में उगी हुई शाखा और पत्ता वर्षा और वसन्त में ग्रहण करने योग्य है।
english: Of these, the branch and leaf (śākhā, palāśa), recently grown, are to be taken in the rainy season and in spring.
notes: 'palāśa' is taken as 'leaf'. The singular neuter dvandva 'śākhāpalāśam' is read as 'branch and leaf' (collective). The relative clause of line 05.08.13 appears to complete here.

hindi: ग्रीष्म में जड़ें, या शिशिर में जिनके पत्ते झड़ चुके और उग आए हैं उनके।
english: In summer, the roots; or in the cold season (śiśira), of those whose leaves have fallen and sprouted.
notes: Elliptical: 'grāhyāṇi' (to be taken) carried over from 14. 'śīrṇaprarūḍhaparṇānām' is ambiguous (those whose leaves are fallen and grown again, or whose fallen leaves have been replaced); the literal rendering is kept. Subject of the genitive is left open in the Sanskrit.

hindi: शरद में छाल, कन्द और क्षीर यानी दूध।
english: In autumn: bark, tuber (kanda) and milk (kṣīra).
notes: Elliptical ('grāhyāṇi' carried). 'kṣīra' is 'milk'; in a plant context it probably means the milky latex of the plant (probable, not stated in the line).

hindi: हेमन्त में सार यानी सम्भवतः काठ का भीतरी भाग।
english: In winter (hemanta): the sāra (essence, core; probably heartwood).
notes: Elliptical ('grāhyāṇi' carried). 'sāra' = essence, core; 'heartwood' is the usual sense for a woody plant (probable).

hindi: ऋतु के अनुसार फल और फूल।
english: Fruit and flower according to the season.
notes: Elliptical ('grāhyam' carried). 'yathartu' is read as 'yathā ṛtu'.

hindi: दूसरे फिर कहते हैं।
english: Others, again, say:
notes: Introduces the next view (line 05.08.20). 'punar' is here 'again' as an introducing particle ('however'); the line leaves the content to the next unit.

hindi: सौम्य औषध सौम्य ऋतुओं में, आग्नेय आग्नेयों में। इस प्रकार वे अविकृत और अधिक पूर्ण रस और वीर्य वाले होते हैं।
english: Saumya (gentle) medicines (auṣadha) in the saumya seasons, āgneya (fiery) ones in the āgneya (ones). Thus (they) become unspoiled, with fuller taste (rasa) and potency (vīrya).
notes:
line 05.08.20: Elliptical: 'grāhyāṇi' (to be taken) carried over. The text does not name which seasons are saumya or āgneya, so none is named here. 'auṣadha' (medicine) is the printed form.
line 05.08.21: 'āpūrṇatara' is a comparative: 'fuller'. 'avyāpanna' = not spoiled, not damaged. Subject (the herbs) understood.

lines_deva: अथ मंगलाचारकल्याणवृत्तिः शुचिः शुक्लवासाः संपूज्य देवतामश्विनौ गोब्राह्मणांश्च कृतोपवासः प्राङ्मुखउदङ्मुखो वा गृह्णीयात्
lines_iast: atha maṃgalācārakalyāṇavṛttiḥ śuciḥ śuklavāsāḥ saṃpūjya devatāmaśvinau gobrāhmaṇāṃśca kṛtopavāsaḥ prāṅmukhaudaṅmukho vā gṛhṇīyāt
hindi: तब मंगल आचार और कल्याणकारी वृत्ति वाला, शुद्ध, श्वेत वस्त्र पहने हुए, देवता, दोनों अश्विनी कुमारों, गौओं और ब्राह्मणों की पूजा करके, उपवास किए हुए, पूर्वमुख या उत्तरमुख होकर ग्रहण करे।
english: Then, of auspicious conduct and good behaviour, clean, in white clothes, having worshipped the deity, the two Aśvins, cows and brahmins, having fasted, facing east or facing north, he should take (it).

text_flags.why: possible: the print runs the two words together without a space; the expected form is the hiatus prāṅmukha udaṅmukho (aḥ before a vowel other than a drops the visarga)

notes: The object of 'gṛhṇīyāt' is not stated (the medicines of the previous units). 'devatām aśvinau' may be two separate objects (the deity; the two Aśvins) or an apposition ('the deity, the two Aśvins'); the first is rendered. english: Among these, having properly examined the taste (rasa), potency (vīrya) and so on of the medicine, and according to the strength of the disease, the patient and so on, he should resort to the preparation of niryāsa and the others (on a conjectural reading of 'kalpanāva nām') and to the dose (mātrā).

text_flags.why: possible: 'āturaādi' leaves a hiatus; sandhi gives 'āturādi'
the word is split by a space and not clear; 'kalpanā' with an unexplained ending 'va nām'

notes: The words 'kalpanāva' and 'nām' are split by a space and unclear; 'kalpanā' (preparation) is a conjecture only and the translation says so. 'mātrā' = dose. 'ādi' = 'and so on'. The sentence tells the physician to base the choice of form and dose on examination.

hindi: और ऐसा कुछ कहते हैं।
english: And thus some say:
notes: Introduces the quotation of lines 05.08.46 and 05.08.47.

lines_deva: मात्राया न व्यवस्थांन देहं दोषं बलं वयः
lines_iast: mātrāyā na vyavasthāṃna dehaṃ doṣaṃ balaṃ vayaḥ
hindi: मात्रा की कोई निश्चित व्यवस्था नहीं है; शरीर, दोष, बल, आयु इन सबको और देश तथा काल को विचारकर औषध का प्रयोग करे।
english: There is no fixed rule for the dose (mātrā); the body, doṣa, strength, age Having considered (these) and place and time, he should administer the medicine (bhaiṣajya).

text_flags.why: possible: genitive 'mātrāyāḥ' needs the visarga
possible: anusvāra and 'na' transposed; 'vyavasthāna' (fixed rule) fits the sense

notes:
line 05.08.46: The sentence continues in line 05.08.47 (the accusatives are completed by 'ālocya'). Conjectural reading of 'mātrāyā na vyavasthāṃna' as 'mātrāyāḥ na vyavasthānam' (no fixed rule of dose); an alternative reading with 'na' twice cannot be excluded. Alternative reading of the second flag: 'vyavasthā na' (stray anusvāra) rather than 'vyavasthānam'; the print alone does not decide.
line 05.08.47: Appears to complete the sentence of 46: 'having considered the body, doṣa, strength, age, and place and time, one should administer the medicine'. Taken together the saying is quoted from 'some' (45). 'avacārayet' = 'should administer, apply' (OPEN wording in the glossary).
OPEN (05.08.47) [minor] hindi / इन सबको: Hindi supplies "इन सबको" for the accusatives of 46 with no bracket possible; English marks it "(these)". Suggested: Acceptable; owner may delete.

hindi: इस प्रकार बस, पर्याप्त।
english: Thus, enough.
notes: A closing remark ending the quotation of 'some' and the discussion of dose; 'alam' = enough. Meaning slightly open.

hindi: वह इस प्रकार बुद्धिमानों के ज्ञान के प्रबोध के लिए उपदिष्ट है। जैसे सब वैद्य समझेंगे, वैसे ही उपदेश दिया जाएगा।
english: That has been taught thus, for the awakening of the knowledge of the intelligent. As, however, all physicians will understand, so it will be taught.
notes:
line 05.08.49: 'jñānaprabodhāya' can be 'for awakening knowledge' (in the intelligent) or 'for awakening of their knowledge'; the plain rendering is kept.
line 05.08.50: 'bhiṣajaḥ' is run into the previous word in print ('sarvebhiṣajo'), a spacing matter only. 'vijñāsyanti' is read as a future 'will understand'.

words.gloss: niryāsa (expressed juice; the first of the five preparations, see line 05.08.33)
four (first part of catuṣ-pala; the printed space splits it)

hindi: निर्यास यानी निचोड़े हुए रस की मध्यम मात्रा सम्भवतः चार पल है। कल्क यानी पिसी हुई लुगदी और चूर्ण का एक कर्ष; उसे घोलने में तीन पल।
english: The middle dose of the niryāsa (expressed juice) is, on a conjectural reading, four palas (pala: a unit of weight). Of kalka (paste) and cūrṇa (powder), a karṣa (a unit of weight); three palas for stirring it.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ca tuṣpalaṃ' is printed with a stray space; 'ca' alone gives no sense after 'mātrā', and 'ca'+'tuṣpalaṃ' together read as catuṣpalam 'four palas'

notes:
line 05.08.51: Nominal sentence; the copula is understood. 'niryāsa' is the expressed juice (svarasa) as defined in line 05.08.33 of this chapter; read here as the name of that preparation. The reading 'four palas' depends on joining 'ca tuṣpalaṃ' into catuṣpalam, which is likely but not certain.
line 05.08.52: Elliptical: 'mātrā' (dose) is understood from line 05.08.51 and no verb is supplied. 'tad' is not stated; it most plainly points back to the kalka and cūrṇa, and the text does not say what the three palas are of (liquid is not stated), so the translation adds nothing. 'āloḍana' is stirring up or mixing.

words.gloss: water; half; prastha (a unit of volume); 'in half a prastha of water'

hindi: निर्यूह यानी काढ़े में: एक पल औषध को आधे प्रस्थ जल में चढ़ाकर चौथाई शेष रहने पर उतार ले। शीत यानी ठण्डे अर्क और फाण्ट यानी गरम अर्क में: औषध का एक पल छह और चार पल जल से भिगोया हुआ।
english: For a decoction (niryūha): having put a pala of the drug on (the fire) in half a prastha (a unit of volume) of water, one should take it down when a quarter remains. For śīta (cold infusion) and phāṇṭa (hot infusion): a pala of the drug, steeped with six and with four palas of water.

text_flags.why: possible: 'buṃpalair' is not a word; 'ambupalaiḥ' (with palas of water) fits the sense, and 'aṃbu' may have been misprinted as 'buṃ'

notes: 'iti' closes the rule and is left untranslated. 'prastha' is a unit of volume (defined in line 05.08.71). 'avatārayet' is 'should take down', the fire being understood. The two numerals 'six' and 'four' fit śīta and phāṇṭa in the order given (six for śīta, four for phāṇṭa); the Sanskrit does not say 'respectively', so the translation does not either. 'āsuta' is taken as 'steeped'. Orthography: 'ārddha' in the print is normalised to 'ardha' in w (same for any doubled -rdd-).

lines_deva: स्नेहपाके त्वनिर्दिष्टप्रमाणे समुदितस्य द्रवस्य पादेन स्नेहः प्रयोज्यस्तत्पादेन कल्कः
lines_iast: snehapāke tvanirdiṣṭapramāṇe samuditasya dravasya pādena snehaḥ prayojyastatpādena kalkaḥ

words.gloss: sneha (fat: ghee or oil; standard); cooking

hindi: जिस स्नेहपाक में प्रमाण न बताया गया हो, उसमें कुल द्रव का चौथाई भाग स्नेह यानी घी या तेल प्रयोग करना चाहिए और उसका चौथाई भाग कल्क यानी लुगदी।
english: In sneha-cooking (the cooking of sneha, fat: ghee or oil) where the measure is not stated, the sneha should be used at a quarter of the total liquid, and the kalka (paste) at a quarter of that.
notes: 'tat' in 'tatpādena' is most naturally the sneha (kalka at a quarter of the sneha); it could also be the liquid, and the text does not say which. 'sneha' in the cooking sense is ghee or oil (standard). The verb 'prayojyaḥ' is carried to 'kalkaḥ'.

hindi: अन्य फिर पढ़ते हैं।
english: Others, again, read.
notes: Introduces a different reading of the rule on measures; the object of 'read' is not stated here and the alternative is apparently given in the units that follow.

words.gram: pres. part. √sidh, loc. sg. (or 3 sg. pres.)

hindi: स्नेह के पकते समय शुद्ध जल, काढ़ा और स्वरस यानी निचोड़े हुए रस से क्रम से। कल्क यानी लुगदी का भाग मिलाना चाहिए: चौथा, छठा, आठवाँ।
english: When the sneha is being cooked: with pure water, decoction and expressed juice (svarasa), in order. One should add the portion of the kalka (paste): a fourth, a sixth, an eighth.
notes:
line 05.08.56: Elliptical: no main verb in this unit. 'snehe siddhyati' is read as a locative absolute ('while the sneha is being cooked'). 'niḥkvātha' is a synonym of kvātha (decoction). The instrumentals are taken with the following units, which the sentence seems to continue into; this is not stated as fact.
line 05.08.57: The whole of which these fractions are a part is not stated. Since the previous unit lists three liquids 'in order' (kramāt) and this unit lists three fractions, the two lists may go together in the order given; the text does not say so.

words.gram: 'five onward' (prabhṛti 'beginning with'); adjective of drava or adverbial

hindi: पाँच से आगे, द्रव को अलग से, स्नेह के बराबर ही डालना चाहिए। जिस औषध का कल्प यानी तैयार करने का प्रकार न बताया गया हो, उसे कल्क यानी लुगदी बनाना चाहिए।
english: But from five onward, one should add the liquid separately, just equal to the sneha. A drug whose kalpa (manner of preparation) is not specified, one should make into kalka (paste).
notes:
line 05.08.58: What the 'five' are (liquids, or other things counted) is not stated. 'pṛthak' could also go with 'snehasama' (separately equal to the sneha); the sense is little changed.
line 05.08.59: 'kalpa' is read here as the form of preparation intended for the drug.

hindi: तब एक साथ मिलाकर और चढ़ाकर निर्यूह यानी काढ़े की तरह तैयार करना चाहिए।
english: Then, having mixed (them) together and put (it) on (the fire), one should prepare (it) like a decoction (niryūha).
notes: The objects are not stated; the drug of line 05.08.59 and the sneha are the natural ones but the text does not name them.

lines_deva: तत्र यदाविरमति शब्दः प्रसादमाप्यते स्नेहो यथास्ववर्णगंधरसोपपत्तिर्भैषज्यमंगुलीभ्यां गृह्यमाणमनतिमृद्द्नतिदारुणमनंगुलिग्राहिता च स्यात् स कालस्तस्यावतारणाय
lines_iast: tatra yadāviramati śabdaḥ prasādamāpyate sneho yathāsvavarṇagaṃdharasopapattirbhaiṣajyamaṃgulībhyāṃ gṛhyamāṇamanatimṛddnatidāruṇamanaṃguligrāhitā ca syāt sa kālastasyāvatāraṇāya

words.gloss: as proper to itself; colour; smell; taste; attainment

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √grah, n. nom. sg.

hindi: वहाँ, जब ध्वनि बन्द हो जाए, स्नेह स्वच्छता को प्राप्त हो, अपने-अपने रंग, गन्ध और रस की प्राप्ति हो, और औषध को दो अंगुलियों से पकड़ने पर वह अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार न अधिक मृदु और न अधिक कठोर हो तथा अंगुलियों से चिपके नहीं, तब वह उसे उतारने का समय है।
english: There, when the sound stops, the sneha reaches clarity, there is the attainment of its own proper colour, smell and taste, and the medicine, when held between two fingers, is neither too soft nor too hard and does not stick to the fingers (on an emended reading, see notes): that is the time for taking it down.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mṛddnati' is not a word; 'mṛdv-anati-' (not too soft, not too hard) fits the sense and the two printed d-letters may be a misread 'dv'

notes:
The 'sound' is not further defined. 'āpyate' is a passive form with an accusative ('prasādam'); read as 'the sneha reaches clarity'. 'bhaiṣajyam' is the medicine (not further defined; the kalka is the natural referent), the object judged by the finger test. The reading 'neither too soft nor too hard' rests on the emendation in text_flags. Orthographic note: 'anaṅguli-' is written with anusvara in the print.
OPEN (05.08.61) [minor] gram / āpyate: Passive of ā-√āp with a nominative subject (snehaḥ) and an accusative (prasādam) is irregular; the sense is middle ('reaches'). Possible original 'āpadyate' or 'āpnoti', not certain. Left as printed. Suggested: Keep; owner may add a text_flag 'possible' if a second witness exists.

hindi: और भी।
english: Moreover.
notes: Formula introducing a further rule (a verse follows in the next units).

lines_deva: लेहस्य तंतुमत्ताप्सु मज्जनं सरणं न च
lines_iast: lehasya taṃtumattāpsu majjanaṃ saraṇaṃ na ca
hindi: घृत यानी घी में झाग का शान्त होना; तैल यानी तेल में, फिर, उसका उत्पन्न होना। लेह यानी चाटने की औषध का तन्तुओं से युक्त होना, जल में डूबना और फैलना नहीं।
english: Of ghṛta (ghee), the subsiding of the froth; of taila (oil), however, the arising of that. Of a leha (electuary), the having of threads, sinking in water, and no spreading.
notes:
line 05.08.63: Elliptical: the sign for taking the sneha down is understood from the context (previous unit); no verb is supplied.
line 05.08.64: Elliptical: the sign of readiness is understood from the context; no verb is supplied. 'apsu' is taken with 'majjanam'; 'no spreading' is not said to be on the water, and the translation does not add it.

lines_deva: अथावतार्य शीतीभूतमहतेन वाससा परिपूय शुचौ दृढे कलशे समासिच्यापिधानेन वा पिधाय शुक्लेन वस्त्रपट्टेनावच्छाद्य सूत्रेण सुबद्धमनुगुसं शुचौ देशे सुस्थितं स्थापयेत्
lines_iast: athāvatārya śītībhūtamahatena vāsasā paripūya śucau dṛḍhe kalaśe samāsicyāpidhānena vā pidhāya śuklena vastrapaṭṭenāvacchādya sūtreṇa subaddhamanugusaṃ śucau deśe susthitaṃ sthāpayet
hindi: फिर उतारकर, ठण्डा हो जाने पर, नए वस्त्र से छानकर, शुद्ध और दृढ़ कलश में उँडेलकर, ढक्कन से बन्द करके या सफेद वस्त्र की पट्टी से ढककर, सूत से भली-भाँति बँधा हुआ और सम्भवतः सुरक्षित, उसे शुद्ध स्थान पर भली प्रकार टिकाकर रखे।
english: Then, having taken it down and (it) having become cool, having strained it through a new (ahata) cloth, having poured it into a clean, firm jar (kalaśa), having closed it with a lid or covered it with a white strip of cloth, well tied with thread and, on a conjectural reading, well protected, one should keep it well placed in a clean place.

text_flags.why: possible: 'anugusaṃ' is not a word; 'anuguptam' (protected) fits, and a dropped 'pta' ligature printed as 'sa' is a likely scan error (the same pattern may explain 'vyāsā' in line 05.08.96)

notes: The object of every action is not stated; it is the prepared sneha. The first 'vā' in the print sits after 'apidhānena' (lid), the second is separate: read as 'with a lid, or covered with a white cloth strip'. 'ahata' is taken as 'new, unused' (literally 'not struck'). 'anuguptam' is conjectural. The adjectives 'subaddham', 'anuguptam', 'susthitam' are read of the covered jar (or its contents).

words.gloss: aṃśya (a minute unit; not defined in the text)

words.gram: nom. sg. (f.? cf. tāḥ in line 05.08.67)

hindi: परिमाण फिर: छह अंश्य एक मरीचि हैं।
english: As for measure, again: six aṃśya are a marīci (a minute unit of measure).
notes:
The copula is understood. 'aṃśya' and 'marīci' are tiny units of measure; the text does not define them beyond this equation, and 'marīci' is not here the pepper (maricha). The form 'aṃśyaḥ' is as printed and the word is not otherwise known to me, so its exact stem is uncertain.
OPEN (05.08.66) [minor] text_flags / ṣaḍaṃśyo: Draft admits aṃśya is unattested to it as a unit and the stem uncertain but sets no flag. The word is probably a corrupt or unusual reading (other tiny-measure lists name aṇu or trasareṇu steps before marīci); no safe correction can be proved from the print. Suggested: Owner decision: keep as printed; add a 'possible' text_flag only if a second witness shows the unit name.
OPEN (05.08.66) [minor] hindi / एक मरीचि: OWNER DECISION: Hindi 'एक' renders the singular (marīciḥ) as an indefinite article; dropping it makes the Hindi read as 'they are six X'. Kept in all of 66-70, 85.

words.gloss: sarṣapa (mustard seed, Brassica species; standard; here a unit of measure)

hindi: वे छह एक सर्षप यानी सरसों हैं।
english: Those six are a sarṣapa (mustard seed; here a unit of measure).
notes: Copula understood. 'tāḥ' is feminine plural and refers back to the marīci of the previous unit (so marīci is treated as feminine here).

words.gloss: taṇḍula (rice grain; Oryza sativa, standard; here a unit of measure)

hindi: वे आठ एक तण्डुल यानी चावल हैं।
english: Those eight are a taṇḍula (rice grain; here a unit of measure).
notes: Copula understood; 'te' (masculine) refers to the sarṣapas of the previous unit.

words.gloss: dhānyamāṣa (a small unit of weight; lit. 'grain-māṣa')

hindi: वे दो एक धान्यमाष हैं।
english: Those two are a dhānyamāṣa (a small unit of weight; literally 'grain-māṣa').
notes: Copula understood; the two taṇḍulas of the previous unit. 'māṣa' is also the name of a bean; the text uses it here as part of a unit name only.

words.gloss: yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare; standard; here a unit of measure)

hindi: वे दो एक यव हैं।
english: Those two are a yava (barley; here a unit of measure).
notes: Copula understood; the two dhānyamāṣas of the previous unit.

words.gloss: aṇḍikā, māṣaka, śāṇa, karṣa, pala, kuḍava, prastha, āḍhaka, droṇa, vaha (named units of weight or volume)

hindi: इसके बाद चार गुना वृद्धि से अण्डिका, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार माषक, शाण, कर्ष, पल, कुडव, प्रस्थ, आढक, द्रोण और वह माने जाते हैं।
english: After this, by fourfold increase, the aṇḍikā, māṣaka and śāṇa (on a conjectural reading), karṣa, pala, kuḍava, prastha, āḍhaka, droṇa and vaha are reckoned.

text_flags.why: possible: 'maṣākaṣāṇa' is not a word; 'māṣaka-śāṇa' (both named in lines 05.08.73 and 05.08.74) fits; the order of the units rises by fourfold steps

notes: The names are the list of units; the text does not say here which is bigger than which except 'by fourfold increase'. 'vaha' may be read 'vāha' (a cartload measure); the print has the short vowel. 'māṣaka-śāṇa' is a conjectural restoration of the printed 'maṣākaṣāṇa'.

hindi: धरण फिर पल का दसवाँ भाग है।
english: The dharaṇa, however, is a tenth part of a pala.
notes:
Read as 'a tenth part of a pala'. The compound could in principle be read 'ten parts', but 'tenth part' is the plainer reading; other texts may give a different value for dharaṇa, which is not used here.
OPEN (05.08.72) [minor] english / a tenth part of a pala: Reading of pala-daśa-bhāga as 'one tenth of a pala' is the plain idiom (cf. ṣaḍbhāga 'one sixth'), but dharaṇa values differ across texts. Fine as drafted; owner to confirm against another witness if one exists.

words.gloss: of the māṣaka (a unit of weight)
kola (a name of the unit; also the name of the jujube fruit)

hindi: माषक के पर्याय हेम और धानक हैं। दो शाण के: क्षुद्र, कोल और वटक।
english: The synonyms of the māṣaka (a unit of weight) are hema and dhānaka. Of two śāṇas: kṣudra, kola and vaṭaka.
notes:
line 05.08.73: 'paryāya' is singular in the print; read of both names.
line 05.08.74: Elliptical: 'paryāya' (synonyms) is understood from line 05.08.73; no verb is supplied. 'kola' also names a fruit (jujube) and 'vaṭaka' a small cake or pellet; here they are unit names only.

lines_deva: कर्षस्य सुवर्णमक्षं पिचुर्बिडालपदकं पाणितलं तिंदुकं कवलग्रहः षोडशिका च
lines_iast: karṣasya suvarṇamakṣaṃ picurbiḍālapadakaṃ pāṇitalaṃ tiṃdukaṃ kavalagrahaḥ ṣoḍaśikā ca

words.gloss: of the karṣa (a unit of weight)
suvarṇa (a name of the unit; lit. 'gold')
picu (a name of the unit; lit. 'cotton')
cat; foot (biḍālapadaka, a name of the unit)
hand; palm (pāṇitala, a name of the unit)

hindi: स्नेहपाक तीन प्रकार का है: मन्द, चिक्कण यानी चिकना और खर-चिक्कण। मन्द तब, जब किट्ट यानी तलछट कल्क के समान हो; चिक्कण तब, जब वह मदन यानी सम्भवतः मोम के समान हो।
english: Sneha-cooking is of three kinds: manda (mild), cikkaṇa (smooth) and khara-cikkaṇa (hard-smooth). Manda when the residue (kiṭṭa) is like the kalka; cikkaṇa when it is like madana (probably wax).
notes:
line 05.08.91: 'khara-cikkaṇa' is taken as 'hard (and) smooth'; the exact sense of the compound is not defined in the text.
line 05.08.92: 'madana' is taken as wax (probable); the word also names a tree (Randia) and the god of love, but wax fits the comparison of a smooth, firm residue. 'kiṭṭa' is the residue or sediment in the pan. 'it' in the second half is the same residue.

hindi: अन्तिम वह, जब थोड़ा बैठता है और काला रहता है। इसके आगे जला हुआ होता है, उसे निकालना चाहिए; कच्चा तो अग्निसाद करने वाला यानी पाचन-अग्नि को क्षीण करने वाला होता है।

text_flags.why: possible: 'āmāḥ' (plural) does not fit the singular sense; 'āmaḥ' (raw) with a short vowel is expected

notes:

The subject throughout is the sneha being cooked, understood from the preceding units. 'agnisāda' is a standard term for the weakening of digestive fire.

english: Mild (mṛdu) for nasya (nasal administration), hard (khara) for abhyaṅga (anointing, oil massage), and cikkaṇa for drinking and for basti (enema). The earth is for the most part pervaded by the mountains Himavat and Vindhya (on a conjectural reading, vyāptā).

english: Thus, in the Aṣṭāṅgasaṅgraha composed by the venerable teacher Vāgbhaṭa, son of the venerable Siṃhagupta, the fifth section, the Kalpasiddhisthāna, is complete.
notes: GROUPING: this is the colophon of the whole fifth part, not a verse; it is typed as a verse in the input. The part is called Kalpasiddhisthāna here (kalpa, siddhi, sthāna), which this study calls Part 5 (Kalpasthāna). The name Vāgbhaṭa is given with the honorific 'ācārya' (teacher), and the author as the son of Siṃhagupta, as the print says; nothing further is added. The printed title Kalpasiddhisthāna is probably the genuine title of the fifth sthāna of this work (which has Kalpa and Siddhi chapters in one sthāna); the study's label 'Kalpasthāna' is shorthand.
